title: A developer console
description:
Most games built with ImGui have a developer console: a text field where you type `god`, `give gold 500` or `teleport 12 40`, with history and Tab completion. ImGui gives you the text field and callbacks (lesson 2.02); write the logic behind them.

```cpp
class Console
{
public:
    void addCommand(const std::string& name, std::function<std::string(const std::vector<std::string>&)> run);
    std::string execute(const std::string& line);        // runs a line, returns what to print
    std::string historyUp(const std::string& current);    // Up arrow: an older line
    std::string historyDown(const std::string& current);  // Down arrow: a newer line
    std::string complete(const std::string& current);     // Tab
    const std::vector<std::string>& log() const;          // everything printed so far
};
```

**Executing** (`execute`):

- Split the line into words on spaces; a part in double quotes is one word without its quotes (`say "hello there"` gives `say`, `hello there`). Empty input does nothing and returns `""`.
- The first word is the command name, matched without regard to case. Run it with the remaining words and return what it returns.
- An unknown command returns `Unknown command: <name>`.
- Add `> ` plus the line to the log, then the result if it is not empty. Add the line to the history unless it is the same as the most recent history entry.
- `help` is built in: it returns all command names, sorted, joined with `", "`.

**History** (`historyUp`, `historyDown`): like a terminal. Up from the edited line shows the newest history entry, then older ones; it stops at the oldest. Down goes back towards newer entries, and past the newest returns to the line that was being typed before Up was first pressed (the `current` argument at that first Up). `execute` resets the position.

**Completion** (`complete`): complete the first word only, against the command names (and `help`):

- if exactly one name starts with it (ignoring case), return that name followed by a space;
- if several do, return their **longest common prefix** (in lower case), or the input unchanged if that is no longer than the input, and add a log line listing the candidates sorted, joined with `"  "`;
- if none do, return the input unchanged.
hints: Splitting: walk the characters with a flag for "inside quotes". A space outside quotes ends a word; a quote toggles the flag and marks that a word exists even if it ends up empty.
History: `-1` means "not browsing". The first Up saves the current text, so Down past the newest entry can give it back.
requirements: Quoted words survive as one argument.
History never stores the same line twice in a row, and Down returns to what was being typed.
Tab completes a unique command and lists the candidates when several match.
Unknown commands are reported, never thrown.
stretch: Hook it up to ImGui: an `InputText` with `EnterReturnsTrue | CallbackHistory | CallbackCompletion`, whose callback calls `historyUp`/`historyDown`/`complete` and replaces the buffer with `DeleteChars` and `InsertChars` (look them up in the console example in imgui_demo.cpp).
